job.title: HR Recruitment Consultant
job.description:
For over fifteen years, Tandem Partners has built a trusted reputation for delivering outstanding results by putting people at the centre of everything we do. With a focus on quality, genuine relationships and integrity, we partner with the HR profession to shape exceptional careers and build high performing teams.  Collectively, our team's wealth of experience surpasses that of any other HR recruitment firm.  
 
We work alongside HR leaders to truly understand their business needs and support candidates in building meaningful careers. Our team are known for their expert HR knowledge, genuine care and ability to deliver tailored solutions with our clients nationally.  We love nothing more than to work together with organisations to build thriving workplaces through evolving HR teams.
 
 
Why Join Tandem Partners?
 
We believe your career should challenge you, support your goals and be fun
 
At Tandem Partners, you'll join a team culture that is:
 
  • Collaborative and supportive - open communication, trust and teamwork are at our core
  • Positive and high performing - we celebrate wins, embrace challenges and make work enjoyable
  • Growth-oriented - we invest in the best tools, professional development and ongoing support to help you succeed
 
Here, you'll make a visible impact, your hard work will be recognised and your career will progress without limitation.
 
The Role
 
Due to continued growth, we are seeking a motivated HR Recruitment Consultant to join our Selection Practice in Melbourne.  We are looking for someone who wants to combine a focus on providing outstanding service as a Talent Partner, with a genuine interest in connecting the HR Community.
 
In this role, you'll:
 
  • Partner with leading organisations hiring across all areas of HR
  • Manage end-to-end recruitment processes while building genuine long-term relationships
  • Work with best-in-class technology and receive full administrative support, so you can focus on being Customer facing
  • Continuously develop your skills in a supportive, professional and forward-thinking environment
  • Play a key part in facilitating opportunities for bringing the community together through events and networking
 
What You'll Bring
 
To thrive with us, you will bring:
 
  • A tertiary qualification in HR or a related discipline and a genuine interest in the HR Profession
  • Experience in a sales or business development role 
  • Excellent customer service skills and the ability to build strong professional relationships
  • A proactive, resourceful mindset with strong candidate assessment skills
  • The ability to juggle multiple priorities while maintaining quality and care
  • Tenacity, resilience and drive to succeed to in a high paced environment
 
What's in It for You?
 
We believe in rewarding the effort you put in. Joining Tandem Partners means:
 
  • Autonomy with support - the freedom to work your way backed by a collaborative team
  • Recognition and reward - your achievements are valued and celebrated
  • Varied opportunities and access to an unparalleled network 
  • Career growth without limitation
If you are confident that your experience reflects the above criteria, please apply online quoting ref No. 3961552
Should you have any questions please contact Clare Johnston at clare@tandempartners.com.au

job.title: HR Project Consultant (Workday Optimisation)
job.description:
About the Organisation:

Our client is an established and progressive organisation with a diverse workforce across Australian and international operations. With a strong commitment to operational excellence and continuous improvement, the business has invested significantly in modernising its HR technology and strengthening its people systems capability.

Following the recent implementation of Workday and changes to its payroll technology, the organisation is focused on maximising system functionality, improving workforce reporting and creating more efficient HR processes.

Working within a collaborative People and Culture function, this is an opportunity to contribute specialist technical expertise and deliver tangible improvements across an evolving HR technology environment.

About the Role:

An immediate opportunity exists for an experienced HR Generalist, HR BP, or HR Manager with Workday expertise to join the organisation on an initial 1 to 2 month contract, providing hands-on functional expertise across HR systems, reporting, configuration, and process improvement.

With Workday recently implemented, the business requires an experienced specialist to optimise existing functionality, troubleshoot outstanding system issues, enhance reporting capabilities and improve operational efficiency.

Working closely with the People and Culture team, including HR Business Partners and payroll stakeholders, you will take ownership of key systems improvements and deliver practical solutions that strengthen HR service delivery.

Key responsibilities will include:
  • Review, configure and optimise existing Workday functionality, identifying opportunities to improve system performance, usability and operational effectiveness.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve HRIS issues, providing practical technical solutions to address current system challenges.
  • Develop, enhance and maintain Workday reports and dashboards, improving the accuracy, accessibility and usefulness of workforce information.
  • Review existing HR reporting processes, identifying opportunities to reduce manual administration and streamline recurring reporting requirements.
  • Support HR data integrity and quality, identifying inconsistencies and improving the reliability of information across HR and payroll systems.
  • Work collaboratively with payroll stakeholders to investigate system issues and support improvements to payroll-related processes, including the ADP environment.
  • Identify and implement opportunities to improve HR process efficiency, workflows, and utilisation of existing technology.
  • Partner with HR Business Partners and other stakeholders to understand operational requirements and translate these into practical system improvements.
  • Provide specialist systems advice, guidance and knowledge transfer to strengthen internal HRIS capability.
  • Support ongoing systems stabilisation and continuous improvement, ensuring solutions are practical, sustainable and aligned with business requirements.
This is a delivery-focused opportunity requiring someone who can quickly understand an existing systems environment, identify priorities and independently implement improvements within a relatively short timeframe.

About You:

You have a strong HR generalist, partnering or management background or a HRIS Specialist background, and are highly proficient with Workday, and can combine strong functional systems expertise with a practical understanding of HR operations, reporting and payroll processes.

You enjoy working directly within systems, solving problems and finding opportunities to improve functionality and efficiency. Comfortable operating independently, you bring a proactive approach, strong analytical capability and the ability to engage effectively with HR and business stakeholders.

To be successful, you will bring:
  • Experience working in a HR team as a HR generalist, business partner, or HR manager, or a HRIS specialist with strong recent experience and knowledge of Workday, including hands-on functional configuration, system administration, troubleshooting and optimisation.
  • Strong Workday reporting capability, including experience developing reports, dashboards and workforce analytics.
  • Experience supporting HR systems following implementation, including identifying and resolving functionality, configuration and data-related challenges.
  • A sound understanding of HR operations, processes and the employee lifecycle.
  • Experience working with payroll systems and an understanding of the interaction between HRIS and payroll processes. ADP experience would be highly regarded.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify and deliver HR process improvements, streamline workflows and reduce manual administrative activities.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate complex systems issues and develop practical solutions.
  • Experience partnering with HR Business Partners, payroll teams and other stakeholders to translate business requirements into systems improvements.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to explain technical information to nontechnical audiences.
  • A proactive, organised and delivery-focused approach, with the ability to work autonomously and make an immediate contribution.
Additional Requirements/Benefits:
  • Initial 1 to 2 month contract with the opportunity to deliver immediate and measurable improvements.
  • Competitive daily contract rate commensurate with specialist Workday experience.
  • Sydney CBD-based role with regular office attendance and some flexibility in working arrangements.
  • Open to part-time arrangements of approximately 2 to 3 days per week for the right contractor. 
  • Opportunity to work with a collaborative and supportive People and Culture team.
  • Exposure to an evolving HR technology environment incorporating Workday and payroll systems.
  • High degree of autonomy and ownership of systems improvements and deliverables.
  • Opportunity to make a visible impact through improved reporting, systems functionality and operational efficiencies.
Why Apply?

This is an excellent opportunity for a technically capable Workday specialist who enjoys getting into the detail, solving problems and delivering meaningful improvements.

Rather than managing a lengthy transformation program, you will have the opportunity to make an immediate impact, applying your expertise to optimise existing technology, strengthen reporting capabilities and improve how HR systems support the business.

You'll join a collaborative team that values specialist knowledge, initiative and practical solutions, with the flexibility of a short-term contract and the opportunity to deliver tangible results.

How to Apply:

If you are confident that your experience reflects the above criteria, please apply online.

Should you have queries or would like to sense-check your alignment, please contact Matthew Saitta by email at matthew@tandempartners.com.au or call 02 8045 2923.

job.title: People Partner, Operations
job.description:
An opportunity for an experienced HR Business Partner to take ownership of the people agenda for a large, operationally complex national workforce.

Partnering closely with three senior business leaders, you will support an employee population of approximately 4,000 across a geographically dispersed, multi-site environment. You will also lead and develop a team of three People Advisors who manage much of the day-to-day people partnering activity within their respective business areas.
 
This is a senior partnering role with a strong focus on understanding business challenges, using workforce and business data to identify priorities, and translating these into practical people strategies. Key areas include workforce and succession planning, organisational design and change, leadership capability, engagement and talent strategy.

The Role
  • Partner with senior operational leaders on their people, workforce and capability priorities.
  • Lead, coach and develop a team of three People Advisors.
  • Develop workforce plans and strengthen succession and talent pipelines.
  • Lead organisational design, restructuring and significant change activity.
  • Identify leadership capability gaps and support the development of stronger people leaders.
  • Use workforce and business data to diagnose issues and build evidence-based recommendations and business cases.
  • Maintain appropriate oversight of employee and industrial relations matters, working alongside specialist workplace relations capability.
  • Help mature a recently introduced people partnering model in an environment undergoing significant change.
About You
 You will be an experienced HR Business Partner or People Partner who has previously led and developed HR/People team members. This is not intended as a first step into people leadership.

You will bring:
  • Senior business partnering experience within a large, complex and multi-site operating environment.
  • Experience supporting high-volume or frontline workforces.
  • Previous responsibility for leading and developing HR Business Partners, HR Advisors or similar.
  • Strong executive-level stakeholder management and the confidence to challenge, advise and influence.
  • Experience across workforce planning, organisational design, change and talent.
  • Sound employee and industrial relations knowledge, ideally including exposure to multiple awards or enterprise agreements and union relationships.
  • The ability to work with autonomy, establish priorities and operate effectively through change.

job.title: Senior HR Advisor
job.description:
Like your HR roles with a bit of variety? This one has plenty.
  
We’re looking for a hands-on Senior HR Advisor who enjoys being close to the business, building genuine relationships with leaders and getting stuck into the people challenges that come with a busy operational environment.

If you enjoy HR that gets you out from behind the desk and into the business, this could be a great next move.

job.title: People & Culture Lead
job.description:
About the Organisation:

This technology-enabled organisation operates a market-leading digital consumer platform across Australia and New Zealand, with a well-known and established brand.

As a smaller, entrepreneurial business, it offers the opportunity to work close to the business and its leadership, with broad exposure, a fast pace and considerable autonomy.

The culture is down-to-earth, collaborative and relationship-driven, with a flat structure where people are trusted to take ownership, influence outcomes and make a genuine impact.
 
About the Role:
 
Reporting to the Group COO, you will step into a highly visible, hands-on People & Culture Lead role, taking ownership of the P&C function during a period of parental leave and partnering closely with the Senior Leadership Team.

Leading a People & Culture Coordinator, you will operate as a true HR generalist and trusted adviser, managing complex employee matters and working across employee and industrial relations, organisational change and broader people initiatives.

With significant autonomy, you will translate business priorities into practical, commercially grounded people solutions, maintain continuity across the function and support a high-performance environment. You will also play a role in technology-enabled workplace change, evolving workflows and employee communications.
 
About You:

You will be a commercially minded HR generalist who enjoys variety, autonomy and being close to the business. Your background may be as a People & Culture Business Partner, HR Manager or senior HR generalist, but most importantly, you will have the breadth and confidence to step in, take ownership and quickly become a trusted adviser across the organisation.

Strong Australian ER/IR capability is essential, alongside hands-on experience in organisational change and coaching leaders through complex people matters. Exposure to New Zealand employment legislation would be highly desirable.

This environment will suit someone who is comfortable with pace, ambiguity and an entrepreneurial way of working. You will communicate clearly, exercise strong commercial judgement and have the confidence to constructively challenge senior stakeholders when required.

Previous experience within an SME, founder-led, digital, technology or commercially driven environment would be highly advantageous.

Experience leading or implementing AI-driven initiatives would also be highly regarded.
 
Additional Requirements/Benefits:
  • This is a full-time, 12-month maximum-term contract based in Sydney, with the possibility of extension.
  • The organisation operates a hybrid working model, with a minimum of 3 days per week in the Sydney office. Additional office attendance may occasionally be required for business priorities.
  • The preferred start is as soon as possible, ideally during December 2026.
  • Immediately available candidates are preferred, although strong candidates with notice periods will be considered. 
Why Apply?

This opportunity will suit a commercial, hands-on HR generalist who thrives on being close to the business, influencing executive decision-making and translating priorities into practical people outcomes.

Over the contract period, you will have the opportunity to make an immediate contribution across complex ER, organisational change, workforce planning, leadership advisory and core P&C operations, with significant autonomy and visibility across the organisation.

How to Apply:

If you are confident that your experience reflects the above criteria, please apply online.

For a confidential discussion or to sense-check your suitability, contact Matthew Saitta at matthew@tandempartners.com.au or on 02 8045 2923.

This organisation operates within a complex, fast paced and commercially driven environment. With an ambitious agenda underway, the organisation is reshaping capabilities and ways of working to support sustainable growth and stronger business performance.

The team offers a supportive environment with clear strategic direction, autonomy and an expectation that experienced professionals will take ownership and confidently drive outcomes.

About the Role:
This position will report to the Head of People & Culture and partner with leadership teams across corporate functions. You will play a central role in helping established and emerging leaders navigate change and workforce readiness activity. 

You will act as a trusted adviser to senior stakeholders, translating business priorities into commercially focused people strategies. The role will lead organisation design activity while supporting leaders to embed new operating models and ways of working.

You will coach leaders through ambiguity, build practical change capability and ensure initiatives are implemented with clarity, engagement and minimal disruption.

The portfolio also includes succession planning, talent management, leadership development, senior recruitment, remuneration and employee relations matters. You will use workforce data, employee feedback and commercial insight to identify capability gaps, strengthen decision making and monitor the effectiveness of people initiatives.

About You:
You are a degree qualified and seasoned People & Culture professional with strong business partnering experience gained within a large organisation. You bring a strong blend of strategic thinking and practical delivery, with the confidence to influence senior stakeholders while remaining close to implementation.

You have demonstrated experience delivering organisation design and cultural change. You understand how to move from strategy to execution, build leader readiness and operationalise change. You are also comfortable managing sensitive and complex employee and industrial relations matters.

You will have the ability to build credibility with successful, driven stakeholders, work through ambiguity and balance commercial priorities with sound people judgement.

You will be resilient, pragmatic and comfortable taking ownership. Advanced communication, negotiation, coaching and problem solving skills will enable you to challenge constructively, provide clear counsel and establish proactive relationships across the business.  

Why Apply?
The breadth of the portfolio provides exposure to complex change, succession planning, leadership development, culture, employee relations and strategic workforce decisions. For an experienced business partner who enjoys ambiguity, practical transformation and senior stakeholder engagement, this role offers meaningful scope, autonomy and the chance to make a visible impact.

job.title: ER Advisor
job.description:
Full job description 

Opportunity to join a large, complex and evolving organisation with a significant multi-site footprint across Australia. Experiencing a period of growth and organisational change, the business is continuing to mature the way its People function delivers specialist support and capability to its leaders.

A dedicated workplace relations function has recently been established. Working closely with the National Workplace Relations Lead, the Senior Workplace Relations Advisor will play an important role in both delivering high-quality workplace relations support and helping shape how the function operates into the future.

This is a hands-on role encompassing the full spectrum of workplace relations, including complex case management, investigations, performance and conduct matters, fitness for work, industrial instrument interpretation, union engagement and Fair Work Commission matters. The position will provide practical workplace relations advice to leaders and People teams, balancing legislative requirements, commercial and operational considerations, risk and employee outcomes.

You will also have the opportunity to influence workplace relations frameworks, policies and processes and build greater capability amongst leaders and the broader People function.

Key responsibilities
  • Manage complex employee and workplace relations matters end-to-end, including misconduct, performance management, grievances, workplace investigations, disciplinary processes and fitness for work matters.
  • Provide pragmatic and technically sound advice on the Fair Work Act, National Employment Standards, modern awards, enterprise agreements, employment contracts and other relevant employment legislation.
  • Partner with leaders to assess workplace relations risk and develop practical, lawful and human-centred solutions.
  • Prepare submissions and represent the organisation in matters before the Fair Work Commission and other relevant tribunals.
  • Coach and guide leaders through workplace relations matters, building their confidence and capability to manage issues effectively and consistently.
  • Draft, review and enhance workplace relations policies, procedures, guidance materials and employment documentation.
  • Identify emerging and systemic workplace relations issues and recommend improvements to processes and ways of working.
  • Interpret enterprise agreements and industrial instruments and contribute to broader industrial relations activity, including union engagement and industrial disputes.
About you
  • Previous experience operating within a large, complex and multi-site environment.
  • Strong knowledge of the Fair Work Act, National Employment Standards, modern awards, enterprise agreements and Australian employment legislation.
  • Experience operating across multiple Australian jurisdictions and providing workplace relations support at scale.
  • Demonstrated experience independently managing complex investigations, performance, conduct and broader employee relations matters.
  • Experience preparing submissions and responding to matters before the Fair Work Commission, including conciliation.
  • Exposure to unionised environments and industrial instruments, with experience supporting enterprise bargaining or broader industrial relations activity advantageous.
  • Experience within healthcare, critical services or other complex and highly regulated operating environments will be highly regarded.
  • Strong relationship-building skills and the ability to establish credibility with stakeholders ranging from frontline leaders through to executives.
  • A pragmatic and commercial approach, with the judgement to assess risk.
  • A collaborative and human-centred style, with the resilience to navigate challenging conversations and competing stakeholder perspectives.
  • The confidence to work autonomously in a fast-paced environment while remaining curious, adaptable and open to new ways of working.
  • Strong written communication, negotiation, conflict resolution and analytical skills.
